title: Review yardsticks: judge each product on its own measure
objectives: State the valuation, return measure, time frame and review questions for each product.
Explain why a closed-ended AIF's early returns can't be judged like a fund NAV.
body_md:
Mutual fund: daily NAV; main return measure XIRR vs benchmark and category; judge over 3–5 years, rolling; key review questions: beating benchmark? Overlap? Allocation on target? PMS: daily valuation, every holding visible; client's own after-fee return vs benchmark (APMI data); judge over 3+ years after fees; key review questions: manager, process, concentration unchanged? AIF: periodic (often quarterly) NAV; unlisted holdings are estimates; for Cat I & II, IRR and multiple of money invested over the fund's life; judge over the full fund life — early years often look weak (the “J-curve”); key review questions: capital drawn and returned as planned? Portfolio companies on track? Fees as expected?

|  | Mutual fund | PMS | AIF |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Valuation | Daily NAV | Daily, every holding visible | Periodic (often quarterly) NAV; unlisted holdings are estimates |
| Main return measure | XIRR vs benchmark and category | Client's own after-fee return vs benchmark (APMI data) | For Cat I & II, IRR and multiple of money invested over the fund's life |
| Judge over | 3–5 years, rolling | 3+ years after fees | The full fund life; early years often look weak (the "J-curve") |
| Key review questions | Beating benchmark? Overlap? Allocation on target? | Manager, process, concentration unchanged? | Capital drawn and returned as planned? Portfolio companies on track? Fees as expected? |

> **Investor takeaway:** Judge each product on the right yardstick and time frame.
example: VC AIF negative after 18 months: expected J-curve territory — review against the fund's plan, not against a mutual fund's NAV.
say: Judge an AIF over its full life, not one statement.
Comparing a closed-ended PE AIF's early returns with a fund NAV is like judging a mango tree in its first year.
never: Judge all three products on 1-year NAV return.
Early AIF weakness always means a bad fund.

o: Early low or negative returns in PE/VC funds before exits
check.why: Early low or negative returns in PE/VC funds before exits. Explain it before the client invests.

check.q: What is the right yardstick for a Category II AIF?
o: IRR and multiple of money over the fund's life
check.why: IRR and multiple of money over the fund's life. Judge over the full life of the fund.

check.q: The right yardstick for a Category II AIF is:
o: IRR and multiple of money over the fund's life
check.why: For Cat I & II, IRR and multiple of money invested over the fund's life.
